name: Chalukya Utsava
description: The flagship annual state festival organized by the Government of Karnataka to commemorate the heritage of the Chalukya dynasty. Held over three days in February across Badami, Pattadakal, and Aihole, featuring classical music recitals, dance dramas against floodlit red sandstone caves, traditional wrestling (Kusti), sports, and handloom exhibitions.
location: Badami (Main Stage), Pattadakal, and Aihole, Bagalkote District
key_events: Classical dance and music performances by national and local artists
Sound and light projections on Badami rock cliffs
Traditional North Karnataka wrestling competitions (Garadi wrestling)
Bagalkote Handloom & Handicraft Exhibition
Heritage procession with folk troupes (Dollu Kunitha, Veeragase, Jagghalige)
inclusive_growth_impact: Generates peak seasonal earnings for local homestays, auto-drivers, guides, handicraft stalls, and street vendors
source: Department of Tourism, Government of Karnataka & Official Bagalkote District Portal

name: Pattadakallu Dance Festival
description: A premier national-level classical dance festival organized annually in January by the Department of Kannada and Culture, Government of Karnataka. Renowned exponents of Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, Kuchipudi, and Mohiniyattam perform against the illuminated 8th-century Virupaksha and Mallikarjuna temples.
location: Pattadakal UNESCO World Heritage Complex, Badami Taluk, Bagalkote District
key_events: National classical dance recitals against temple backdrop
Instrumental jugalbandis and Carnatic/Hindustani vocal concerts
Artisan display stalls for GI handlooms
Special heritage illumination of UNESCO monuments
inclusive_growth_impact: Brings national and international cultural tourists directly to rural heritage villages, stimulating local rural hospitality
source: Department of Tourism, Government of Karnataka

name: Banashankari Temple Jatre (Fair)
description: One of the largest and most historic rural temple fairs in North Karnataka, held in the holy month of Pushya (January-February) on the full moon day (Banada Hunnime). Spanning nearly a month, it combines intense religious devotion with massive rural trade: handloom sarees, agricultural implements, kitchenware, livestock, and traditional entertainment.
location: Banashankari Temple, Cholachagudda, Badami Taluk, Bagalkote District
key_events: Grand Car Festival (Rathotsava) of Goddess Banashankari
Sacred holy bath in Haridra Tirtha kalyani
Vast rural trade fair: thousands of temporary stalls selling Ilkal sarees, Khana cloth, wooden toys, sweets, and utensils
Traditional folk theater (Bayalata / Sannata) and drama company performances
Cattle and agricultural equipment fair
inclusive_growth_impact: Critical economic lifeline for rural artisans, street food vendors, local farmers, transport operators, and folk artists

name: Basava Jayanti Celebrations at Kudala Sangama
description: The auspicious birth anniversary festival of 12th-century philosopher and social reformer Jagadjyothi Basaveshwara, celebrated with immense fervor in April-May (Rohini Nakshatra). Hundreds of thousands of devotees and scholars gather at the river confluence for seminars on social justice, Vachana singing, and mass community dining (Dasoha).
location: Kudala Sangama, Hunagund Taluk, Bagalkote District
key_events: Special prayers and floral offerings at Aikya Mantapa in the river
National Vachana Gayana concerts and discourses by eminent scholars
Inter-caste mass marriage ceremonies adhering to Sharana principles
Universal community meal (Maha Dasoha) served to all pilgrims without distinction of caste, creed, or gender
inclusive_growth_impact: Fosters community inclusion, supports local rural transport, and promotes social harmony principles
source: Kudalasangama Development Board & Official Bagalkote District Portal

name: Pattadakal Virupaksha Car Festival
description: Annual temple chariot festival celebrated at the historic Virupaksha Temple in Pattadakal during March-April. The beautifully decorated wooden ratha (chariot) carrying the deity is pulled by thousands of village devotees along the ancient temple street.
key_events: Procession of the sacred wooden chariot
Traditional folk drum ensembles (Dollu, Halagi)
Rural bazaar of traditional sweets and toys
inclusive_growth_impact: Direct income generation for local village vendors and service providers

name: Ilkal Vijaya Mahantesha Jatre
description: Massive annual festival of the Shri Vijaya Mahantesha Matha in Ilkal. Combines religious ceremonies with the largest regional handloom exhibition, drawing textile traders and families from Karnataka, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.
key_events: Rathotsava of Vijaya Mahantesha Swamiji
Mega Handloom Saree Exhibition and direct-to-consumer sales
Public lectures on handloom revival and spiritual values
inclusive_growth_impact: Direct multi-million rupee revenue injection into local handloom weaver societies and individual artisans
